ContentApprove.description: Approve the current version, identified by its hash.

patch.description: Brands are never deleted; set `status: archived` instead.

post.summary: Create a new draft profile version

patch.description: Approved versions are immutable (409); create a new version instead.

post.summary: Approve a profile version and make it current
post.description: Freezes the version and makes it the brand's only current profile. Approving an older approved version again makes it current (rollback).

post.summary: Register a social account for a brand
post.description: Stores metadata only. Credentials arrive with the token vault (Faz 3).

patch.description: Accounts are not deleted (schedules reference them); set `status: disabled`.

post.description: Stores the file in R2 and records its metadata. Enforces the mime allow-list (415) and per-type size limits (413).

file.description: The file. Allowed types: see ASSET_MIME_RULES.

get.description: Supports `Range` (206) and `If-None-Match` (304) for media playback and caching.

post.summary: Create a content item (draft, no version yet)

patch.description: `title`/`brief` change freely. Changing `caption` or `targetPlatforms` on approved, scheduled or failed content revokes the approval (back to draft, pending schedules cancelled); it is refused (409) while publishing or published.

delete.summary: Delete a content item with its versions
delete.description: Refused (409) while scheduled, publishing or published.

post.summary: Approve the current version by its hash
post.description: The body carries the hash of the version the user looked at. It must equal the current version's hash, otherwise 409 `hash_mismatch` (someone added a newer version). Allowed from draft or in_review; repeating it on approved content with the same hash is a no-op.

Allowed: draft -> in_review, in_review -> draft, approved -> draft (revoke), failed -> draft, failed -> approved (only if the approval still matches). Approval itself uses /approve; scheduling uses /api/schedules.

get.summary: List versions (newest first, without slide HTML)

post.summary: Add a version (becomes current; content returns to draft)
post.description: The server computes the content hash. Any approval is cleared and pending schedules are cancelled, because approval is bound to a specific hash. Refused (409) while publishing or published.

get.summary: Get one version with its slides

patch.description: Slides are immutable; neither field changes the content hash.

get.description: WebSocket upgrade. Optional `jobId` (one job) or `brandId` (one brand); neither = all jobs. The server sends `jobs.snapshot` first, then `job.updated` and `presence` frames (schema `JobStreamMessage` in @studio/contract). Clients may send `ping`; reconnect and use the new snapshot after a drop.

post.description: Stores the job as `queued` and notifies the Hub, which dispatches it to the Mac worker now or as soon as one connects (priority desc, then FIFO).

A queued job is cancelled at once. A running job gets `cancelRequestedAt` and stays `running` until the worker confirms (or the cancel grace period passes); follow it on the stream. 409 `invalid_transition` when the job already finished.

200.description: The job after the cancel request.

get.summary: List schedules (by scheduled time, earliest first)

post.summary: Schedule approved content on one social account
post.description: The content must be approved (or already scheduled / failed) and its approval must still match the current version; the schedule freezes that version and hash. The account must belong to the content's brand, not be disabled, and its platform must be one of the content's target platforms. Moves the content to `scheduled`.
Only `pending` schedules can be cancelled. When the content has no other active schedule it returns from `scheduled` to `approved`.

get.summary: List publish attempts for a schedule (oldest first)

200.description: A page of publish log entries.

get.description: Online/offline, last seen, the jobs running now and the queue length. The same object is pushed as `presence` frames on /api/jobs/stream.
